ruby.source:
# Theme preview: symbols, interpolation and methods.
class Palette
  attr_reader :name, :count

  def initialize(name, count: 42)
    @name = name
    @count = count
  end

  def describe
    "Theme: #{name} (#{count})"
  end
end

palette = Palette.new("Maru", count: 42)
puts palette.describe if palette.count.positive?

php.source:
<?php
// Theme preview: types, properties, functions and strings.
final class Palette {
    public function __construct(
        public string $name,
        public int $count = 42,
    ) {}

    public function describe(): string {
        return "Theme: {$this->name} ({$this->count})";
    }
}

$palette = new Palette("Maru");
if ($palette->count > 0) {
    echo $palette->describe();
}

bash.source:
#!/bin/bash
# Theme preview: variables, strings and command substitution.
set -eu

name="Maru"
count=42

describe() {
    local label="$1"
    printf 'Theme: %s (%s)\n' "$label" "$count"
}

if [ "$count" -gt 0 ]; then
    describe "$name"
fi

for feature in syntax diff search; do
    printf '%s\n' "$feature"
done

dockerfile.source:
# Theme preview: instructions, arguments and variables.
FROM alpine:3.20 AS preview

ARG THEME=Maru
ENV EDITOR_THEME=${THEME}
WORKDIR /app

COPY ./samples /app/samples
RUN printf 'Theme: %s\n' "$EDITOR_THEME" \
    && mkdir -p /app/output

LABEL org.example.preview="syntax colors"
EXPOSE 8080
USER nobody

ENTRYPOINT ["/bin/sh"]
CMD ["-c", "echo Theme preview"]

make.source:
# Theme preview: targets, variables and shell recipes.
THEME := Maru
COUNT ?= 42
OUTPUT := output

.PHONY: all preview clean

all: preview

$(OUTPUT):
	mkdir -p $@

preview: | $(OUTPUT)
	@printf 'Theme: %s (%s)\n' "$(THEME)" "$(COUNT)"
	@for feature in syntax diff search; do \
		printf '%s\n' "$$feature"; \
	done

clean:
	rm -f $(OUTPUT)/preview.txt

sql.source:
-- Theme preview: keywords, identifiers and literals.
CREATE TABLE palettes (
    id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY,
    name VARCHAR(64) NOT NULL,
    color_count INTEGER DEFAULT 42,
    enabled BOOLEAN DEFAULT TRUE
);

INSERT INTO palettes (id, name)
VALUES (1, 'Maru');

SELECT p.name, COUNT(*) AS total
FROM palettes AS p
WHERE p.enabled = TRUE
  AND p.color_count > 0
GROUP BY p.name
ORDER BY total DESC;
